Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business · Town, shops & places

refund verb and noun

also refunds, give a refund, get a refund, money back, give the money back, pay back, repay, reimburse

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.1.92: sī nōn redderet pecūniam, if he would not give back the money
Liv. 33.13: obsidēs pecūniamque reddī Philippō

pecūniam reddere

verb phrase

give the money back, refund

Latin has no word of its own for it: reddere, give back (see give back), with the money as its object; comedy says argentum reddere.

Examples

  • tū huic argentum redde. hoc jūdicium meum est. — Tū autem in nervō jam jacēbis, nisi mī argentum redditur.

    You, give him his money back: that is my judgment. — And you’ll soon be lying in chains if I don’t get my money back.Plaut. Curc. 717–718

  • sī pāx nōn impetrāta ab senātū foret, obsidēs pecūniamque reddī Philippō receptum est

    it was guaranteed that if the senate did not grant peace, the hostages and the money would be given back to PhilipLiv. 33.13

Other words

  • redhibeō, redhibēre, —, redhibitum — return a faulty purchase (for the price back); of the seller, take it back

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Merc. 419: dīxit sē redhibēre, sī nōn placeat, he said he would take her back if she did not suit; Cic. Off. 3.91 (Lewis & Short)

    A trader’s word: the goods go back to the seller, and the price to the buyer (Lewis & Short).

See also give back, pay, price, receipt, shop.

SourcesLewis & Short: reddo · Lewis & Short: redhibeo
